classification: Conditional public helper input-range and arithmetic contract question; inspected reducer producer is bounded and no supported gameplay failure established.
trace: The current public sneak_succeeds function accepts party_stealth and enemy_awareness as unrestricted u16 values and adds each to an index(1000) draw using ordinary u16 addition. The sampler source states a half-open range, so the intended draw range is 0 through 999. If a caller supplies 65535 and the corresponding draw is nonzero, the sum exceeds u16; the actual overflow response depends on compilation settings. No concrete seed, execution or admitted current caller producing that input was established.

The inspected strategic reducer passes the minimum whole-party sneak score formed from capped_training_rank times 100 and casts to u16. The inspected skill cap clamps aptitude to 0 through 5 and applies min to the training rank, so this producer supplies at most 500. The enemy argument is saturating 200 plus a threat combat stealth u8, at most 455. With draws below 1000, those inspected producer sums remain within u16; the shown reducer path is not evidence of overflow.

The same encounter module uses saturating addition in awareness_from_rolls, which is a different semantic operation. Do not silently equate awareness rolls and sneak contest scores or change deterministic stream behavior; all callers, owner semantics and historical queue aliases remain open.
repair_direction: Trace all actual callers and the intended score domain. If a future authorized repair is warranted, establish a bounded score contract or safe arithmetic at the owner boundary, while preserving valid encounter outcomes and deterministic draw domains. Do not invent a compatibility path.
later_acceptance: After separate repair authorization, exercise admitted lower, upper and invalid score bounds and confirm normal contest outcomes and deterministic replay identity.
